jobs.title: 2027 Finance Placement (Glasgow) at Hilton
jobs.description: Employer: Hilton Expires: 10/20/2026 Exceptional Hospitality Starts with YouAs a participant in our 12-month Corporate Placements Programme in the Finance Department at our Glasgow Corporate Office – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by contributing to the memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.Here’s what you can look forward to as a programme participant:Prepare for a career in hospitality: Embark on a 12-month transformative journey, encompassing a structured framework of learning and development opportunities, business support activities, and ownership of your own project-based initiatives.Gain hands-on operational experience: From day one, you’ll be fully integrated into Team Hilton. Connect with professionals across the business and gain insight into Finance. Take the opportunity to gain insight into at least one other business area, paving the way for valuable future relationships.Work on real-world projects: Apply your skills on the job through business-driven projects to reinforce your learning and gain hands-on experience.Develop your skills through world-class training and support: Access Hilton University’s e-learning modules and business library while building knowledge through business-driven projects.Grow with personalised guidance: Benefit from regular feedback and coaching to ensure your progress is supported at every stage of the programme.Hilton Perks: Including our Go Hilton Team Member Travel Program, which provides you with access to heavily reduced hotel room rates for you, your family & friends. Salary & Benefits: £27,500 gross per annum & private healthcare. Location: At our Glasgow Corporate Office, with some flexibility depending on team and business need. You will benefit from our social area, including a table tennis and pool table. We have good transport links, just a five-minute walk from Central & Queen Street Train Stations, and Buchanan Street Subway. Our Placement OpportunitiesWe have a range of placement opportunities within our highly talented Finance department:Hilton Glasgow Finance Centre of ExcellenceHilton’s Glasgow Finance Centre of Excellence is a great place for individuals looking to gain real-world experience in a global finance environment.All placements will provide exposure to a wide range of corporate finance activities, including journal postings, balance sheet reconciliations, VAT and revenue analysis, audit support, and financial reporting. Placement students will work closely with experienced professionals across various finance functions, contributing to the monthly close process, supporting compliance and control activities, and engaging in continuous improvement initiatives.You’ll gain insight into Hilton’s financial systems and processes, develop your analytical and organisational skills, and build a strong foundation for a career in finance. This is a unique opportunity to be part of a collaborative, fast-paced team within one of the world’s most recognised hospitality brands, where innovation and excellence are at the heart of everything we do.We have opportunities available in:Hotel Accounting.Order-To-Cash (OTC).Process-to-Pay (PTP).Corporate Accounting.Revenue Accounting.US Banking.Record to Report (RTR). UK Payroll & Compliance TeamHilton’s UK Payroll & Compliance Team is part of our wider HR function and is responsible for payroll activities for approximately 7,000 Team Members across 51 Hilton properties. This is a fantastic opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced, high-impact environment where accuracy, collaboration, and meeting deadlines are essential.As an intern in the UK Payroll & Compliance Team, you will develop practical skills in payroll, finance, and compliance, while learning how we ensure our Team Members are paid accurately and on time.What you’ll gain:Practical experience in UK payroll legislation and processes.Exposure to payroll accounting and financial controls.The opportunity to work on meaningful projects and process improvements.Collaboration with international teams and our Global Payroll Services network.Insight into how a global organisation operates behind the scenes.What you’ll be doing:Supporting payroll processing and analysing payroll data.Assisting with reconciliations, general ledger postings, and journal entries.Contributing to balance sheet reconciliations and financial reporting.Supporting HMRC compliance activities, including benefits-in-kind reporting.Completing monthly SOX controls and audit checks.Working closely with internal teams, including our Global Payroll team and Shared Service Centre in Hyderabad. Financial Systems TeamHilton's Financial Systems team is part of our global Finance function. This is a fantastic opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced, high-impact environment where accuracy, collaboration, and delivering against deadlines are key.As a Financial Systems Intern, you'll develop an understanding of Hilton's financial systems and processes while working with teams across Finance, Technology, Global Support and external vendor partners. You’ll build analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills while contributing to system enhancements, process improvements, and global enhancement initiatives that support Hilton’s worldwide operations, creating a strong foundation for a future career in finance, systems, or technology.You'll gain an appreciation of how a global organisation operates behind the scenes through collaboration with international teams and hands-on experience across a range of financial applications. In addition, you'll develop an understanding of financial controls and governance processes while gaining exposure to automation, digital transformation, and emerging AI-enabled finance technologies.What you'll be doing:Supporting user administration activities and system administration tasks in BlackLine, including user access reviews, scheduling imports, organisational structure updates, and country rollouts.Configuring expense types and maintaining override tables.Troubleshooting end-user issues related to system access and functionality & supporting testing activities for system enhancements and new projects.Maintaining training materials and application documentation to ensure they remain accurate and up to date.Participating in project meetings and gaining exposure to system implementations, global rollouts, and enhancement initiatives.Analysing system data and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, user experience, and process effectiveness. What We’re Looking ForWe are seeking individuals who embody the Hilton Values in addition to the following criteria:A current bachelor’s or master’s student completing a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Economics, or other equivalent, that includes a required 12-month year in industry placement.Availability to begin full-time employment on 5th July 2027, for a full-time 12-month placement.You must have the independent right to work in the UK for the full duration of the 12-month placement. Please note that this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route, so we are unable to consider applications from candidates who would require sponsorship. If you hold a visa or status that allows you to work in the UK full-time without sponsorship (e.g. Settled Status, Pre-Settled Status, where a 12-month work placement is a permitted, required & assessed part of your UK University degree, or other independent work permissions), you are welcome to apply.Fluency in English (spoken and written).You should be able to demonstrate a genuine interest in Finance.Able to demonstrate a high level of numerical and analytical capability. Selection ProcessApplications are now open—don’t miss your chance to apply! Submissions close on Tuesday 20th October 2026Our selection process is designed to bring out your best and help us get to know you. It includes:Online assessments.In-person Assessment Centre in our Glasgow Corporate Office (24th November 2026). While the process is rigorous, it’s also the first step in your personal growth journey with Hilton. If selected, you’ll begin developing the skills, connections, and confidence to thrive in your career.To ensure every application receives fair consideration, invitations to the final-stage assessment centre will be issued after applications have closed. Please complete each stage promptly and keep an eye on your inbox for updates.We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing reasonable adjustments for applicants and employees with disabilities. If you require any support or adjustments during the recruitment process or to carry out the essential requirements of the role, please contact us.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Inner Peak
jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 10/21/2026 Marketing Intern: B2B Growth & Digital PresenceInner Peak builds mental health support for students, and we sell it to K-12 districts and universities. The team is small. There is no marketing function yet, and that's why we are hiring you: you'd be building it next to our VP of Sales & Marketing, who you'd report to directly.Worth saying up front, we don't have a playbook to hand you. We're still writing it. Some of what you try is going to flop. That's ok. We are paying you to learn together with us. The work:Build and run a monthly email campaign to actual prospects: superintendents, student services directors, deans of student affairsRun our LinkedIn page. What goes out, how often, who we engage with, how fast the following growsDo the same for Instagram and TikTok, which are earlier and messierSet up and manage paid campaigns on LinkedIn, Meta, and Google. You get a budget and you decide where it goesWrite for school and university administrators, which is a tougher audience than it soundsPut together a monthly rundown of what happened: impressions, engagement, follower growth, cost per lead, what you'd changeBring us channels and ideas we haven't tried. If it's reasonable, we'll fund itYou're probably a good fit if:You're a junior or senior studying marketing, communications, business, or something close to itYou've run a social account for a club, a team, a small business, or yourself, and you can show us the numbersYou've written for an audience that wasn't your friendsYou've poked around in LinkedIn Ads or Meta Ads Manager. Great if you have, not a dealbreaker if you haven'tYou're fine with a plan made Tuesday looking different by ThursdayYou'd rather send us a rough draft on Monday than a perfect one in three weeksPay:$1,000 a month, plus 10% commission on any deal that closes from a lead marketing brought in. So if a campaign you built puts pipeline in front of sales and it closes, you get paid on it. We'd like that commission number to end up bigger than your base.What you get besides the money:You'll finish with campaigns that were yours and metrics attached to them, which gives you something specific to talk about in interviews instead of a vague description of a team you sat near. You'll also get a close look at how a company this size figures out who its buyers are and how to reach them, and steady time with people who have built revenue teams across healthcare, education, and digital commerce.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Nonprofit Accelerator Internship at University Impact
jobs.description: Employer: University Impact Expires: 10/21/2026 Nonprofit Accelerator Internship – UI Charitable Outcomes Lab(Priority Applications Due 9.25.2026) BackgroundUI Charitable helps financial advisors and their clients give more impactfully. We work with ~1,300 families and ~400 financial advisors, and we manage $500+ million in charitable assets. More importantly, we have moved over $350 million out the door to nonprofits and impact investments working to improve the world's most pressing social and environmental issues. Why We Think This Work Matters NowTwo forces are about to reshape philanthropy. The AI boom is creating a new generation of wealth, and the founders and employees holding that ownership are deciding how to structure their giving. Most of them will want to move money out faster than the sector can absorb it. Over the same period, as much as $124 trillion will change hands through 2048, with an anticipated $18 trillion of it going to charity. We are building the infrastructure to turn that money into real improvements in people's lives. The Problem You Will Work on For This InternshipA lot of charitable dollars do not produce the lasting change donors expect. Plenty of funded organizations will never solve the problem they exist to solve, and money alone will not fix that. Most attempts to address this try to change donor behavior, including several of our own. So we are working on the organizations instead. What We Are BuildingEight years of building the infrastructure gives us a direct relationship with thousands of nonprofits our donors already fund. We want to help them become more effective. The closest analogy is a business accelerator for nonprofits, or a private equity operating team. We assess an organization across the core functions of a well-run business, run it through a cohort based program, and reassess later to see what moved. So far we have a literature review, a survey of 150 nonprofits, an analysis of our own data, and some first drafts of our curriculum and a way we will measure the success of the program. We will judge the program by whether those organizations actually improve, not by how many attend. The Eight Functions We want all organizations our donors give to, to have a sound understanding of their outcomes and impact. But in order to do that, you have to be running an effective/efficient organization. We are organizing the program around the functions that separate organizations that grow from organizations that stall. Each intern will own work across multiple of these functions.Fundraising and the growth engine. Treating donor development as a sales pipeline with stages, conversion rates, and follow-up. (Sales, Marketing, and Branding)AI adoption and operations. Where AI can take real work off a five-person staff. Marketing and branding. Making the case for support to people who have never heard of the organization.Board development and governance. What effective boards do, and how to get a board to do it.Program measurement and evaluation. Outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how small organizations can measure honestly without a research budget. (Public Health, Statistics, etc.)Finance, accounting, and internal controls. Who approves spending, who reconciles accounts, and what gets outsourced.Technology and data systems. CRM, donor records, and reporting that does not live in the executive director’s head.Talent and leadership capacity. Hiring, retention, and how a small team allocates the hours it has. Position OverviewWe are hiring two interns to help run a year-long pilot. You will work directly with Gary McHardy (a Rhodes Scholar based in South Africa) and Tanner Mills (Sr. Associate at UI Charitable). The team is small and the program is new, which means you will own real pieces of the work rather than support someone else’s. You will interview nonprofit CEOs, build the assessment instruments, write and deliver curriculum, and sit in on calls with the senior advisors guiding the program. Duties and Responsibilities:Design the curriculum. Build the workshop content, templates, and tools for your assigned functions, covering what the best organizations do and how a five-person staff can actually do it.Deliver it. Run webinars, cohort sessions, and office hours. You will be the one teaching, not just organizing.Drive results at the organizations. Work directly with participating nonprofits to implement what the curriculum covers. The goal is a CRM that exists, a pipeline that gets worked, a board that shows up.Interview nonprofit leaders. Run discovery calls, take structured notes, and turn what you hear into changes to the program.Analyze the data. Segment organizations by size, growth trend, and reported need using assessment results and public financials.Measure our own results and make adjustments. Track baseline and follow-up scores and report the delta honestly, including where we did not move the needle.The above list is not exhaustive; additional tasks will for sure be assigned as necessary. Required Skills/Abilities:Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication. You will be talking with nonprofit executives and delivering material they will read.Analytical Skills: Able to work with survey and financial data, draw conclusions, and present findings clearly and concisely.Project Management Skills: Able to handle several workstreams at once, prioritize, and hit deadlines without being chased.Comfort with Ambiguity: This program does not exist yet. You should be comfortable proposing an approach, testing it, and changing it when it fails.Team Coordination: Work very well with other people as a high output team. Deliver on what you’re responsible for AI Fluency: Regular use of AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis, with the judgment to check the output.Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to break a large, vague problem into pieces someone can actually work on.Humility and a Desire to Learn: A strong interest in understanding UI Charitable’s tools and programs and their role in achieving social impact.Integrity: Keep commitments, admit mistakes, maintain confidentiality where appropriate, and act in the organization’s best interests at all times. Education and Experience:Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree. Business, economics, statistics, public health, public policy, marketing, computer science and communications backgrounds all fit.Coursework, work experience, or genuine interest in at least one of the eight functions listed above. Tell us which one or two in your application.Proficiency with spreadsheets, survey tools, and standard office applications.Prior nonprofit experience is welcome but not required. Physical Requirements:Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The expectation is that candidates would be able to commit 20 hours per week, in person. How to ApplyEmail Tanner at tanner@uicharitable.org with your resume and a short note, under 250 words. Tell us which of the eight functions you would most want to own, why you want to work on this, and about anything you have produced, built, sold, raised, or automated. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYUI Charitable offers fair and equal employment opportunity to all qualified job candidates regardless of age, race, religion, color, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, arrest record, conviction record, physical disability, developmental disability, national origin, membership in the National Guard, state defense force or any other reserve component of the military forces of the United States or Utah, genetic information, marital status, or any legally protected status.

King Jr. and the SUNY Board of Trustees: student success; research and scholarship; diversity, equity, and inclusion; and economic development and upward mobility. This position offers a hands-on opportunity to support the SUNY social media presence through content creation, digital storytelling, and trend analysis. jobs.title: 2027 Investment Services Internship at Point72
jobs.description: Employer: Point72 Expires: 10/22/2026 A Career with Point72’s Investment Services TeamOur Investment Services colleagues are subject-matter experts who excel in their fields, comprise more than half our firm, and are critical to our success. As strategic partners, they support our investment professionals across areas including strategy, operations, finance, technology, compliance, tax, HR and legal. Everyone on every team has the opportunity to make an impact on our business. About the Investment Services InternshipIf you are interested in pursuing a career in the corporate functions of a leading global alternative investment firm, this 10-week summer internship will provide you with valuable, hands-on experience at a complex global firm. You will gain exposure to the fast-paced, competitive hedge fund industry alongside senior professionals dedicated to your success. In addition to the learning and development you'll receive in your day-to-day role with your team, as part of our summer internship program you will:Work alongside your fellow interns and be mentored by experienced professionalsMeet your peers through designated intern programming, volunteer opportunities, and social eventsAttend sessions with senior leaders discussing their expertise and career pathsHave hands-on access to best-in-class tools and resourcesGain exposure to groups and functions with unique responsibilities and perspectives on our industryDevelop your technical, writing, and presentation skills When you apply to our internship program, you will be considered for a variety of teams based on your interests and experience and our business needs. What's RequiredCurrently pursuing a bachelor's degreeInterest in the asset management industryAbility to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a fast-paced environmentStrong attention to detailStrong analytical, writing, verbal communication, and technical skillsDemonstrated ability to work cooperatively with all levels of the teamDemonstrate professionalism and integrity in all interactionsCommitment to the highest ethical standards Team OverviewsCommunicationsThe Corporate Communications team manages the global reputation of Point72 across media relations, external and internal communications, digital content, and brand management. Interns gain exposure to research and content creation - including media monitoring, competitive audits, branded recruiting and digital content, event planning, and bespoke projects - working closely with senior management and functional leaders firmwide. ComplianceThe Compliance team supports the firm's global investment and trading activities by establishing and enforcing the firm’s compliance policies, providing real-time advice, and conducting pre- and post-trade surveillance. Interns will gain exposure to enforcing the Code of Ethics and personal trading programs, liaising with global regulators, maintaining the firm's restricted list, and performing due diligence on research providers, consultants, and trading counterparties. FinanceThe Corporate Finance team provides timely, accurate financial information, advice, and services to business partners across Corporate Accounting, Global Payments, Procurement, FP&A, and Financial Reporting. Interns will gain exposure to day-to-day activities such as the month-end close, investor risk reports, and consolidated monthly financial packages, while sharpening Excel, writing, and presentation skills through intensive mentoring. OperationsThe Trade Support team, part of Operations, supports the operational aspects of trade processing, reconciliation, financing, and reporting for all products across global markets - equities, derivatives, bonds, foreign exchange, and futures. Interns will gain exposure to working with traders and counterparties to resolve trading matters and help provide accurate books and records for the firm on a daily and monthly basis. Strategic ImplementationThe Strategic Implementation team leads complex, cross-functional initiatives that support the growth of Point72's businesses, partnering with Strategy, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Technology. Interns will gain exposure to the end-to-end program cycle —coordinating meetings and deliverables, building project plans and timelines, documenting current state, conducting root cause analysis, and developing playbooks for key activities. StrategyThe Corporate Strategy team is a small, multidisciplinary group reporting to the Chief Operating Officer that identifies, designs, and executes value-creating cross-functional initiatives and engages in new business and special situations. Interns will gain exposure to strategic priorities by supporting analyses on operations, performing quantitative and qualitative research (competitive analysis, industry trends, market conditions), and providing project management support on key initiatives. Regulatory ReportingThe Regulatory Reporting team provides governance across all regulatory filings and obligations globally, including submissions to the SEC, CFTC, NFA, MAS, FCA, SFC, and Kanto Finance Bureau. Interns will gain exposure to filing preparation and submission, execute data reconciliations and exception investigations, partner with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Risk, Technology, and Trading, and help identify automation opportunities that improve accuracy and reduce manual effort. TreasuryThe Treasury team supports the firm's credit and treasury functions across Central Funding, Securities Lending, and Broker Relations—verifying and disputing margin calls, reporting on counterparty exposure, investing excess cash, and negotiating margin terms with prime brokers and derivative counterparts. Interns will gain hands-on exposure to a wide range of financial instruments across global markets while working alongside senior treasury professionals. Human CapitalThe Human Capital team serves as trusted business partners and advisors within the Point72 community, committed to driving a distinctive culture that values collaboration, innovation, and adaptive performance. Interns will gain exposure to day-to-day HR operations including onboarding, employee records, and benefits administration, along with recruiting and interview coordination, HR reporting and project work, and compliance and privacy best practices for handling confidential information. LegalThe Legal team works to deliver exceptional legal services in a manner that promotes the firm’s performance with the utmost integrity and supports all Point72 groups globally with practical advice on a variety of complex legal and regulatory matters in an ever-changing, dynamic environment. Interns will gain exposure to regulatory filings and obligations, drafting and updating firm policies, due diligence reviews, and industry best-in-class automation and data visualization tools that support the department. About Point72Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry's brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people's long-term growth. For more information, visit https://point72.com/.The annual base salary is $75,000 (USD) which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.

jobs.title: Summer Analyst Corporate and Leveraged Finance at Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank Expires: 10/22/2026 Summer Internship:Credit Agricole CIB hosts a 10-week internship. This internship provides students with the opportunity to obtain relevant professional experience, network with colleagues and senior employees, and learn about the investment banking (IB) industry. Our internship includes one structured week of technical and functional training, on the desk work, networking/educational events, and a formal evaluation process. Different events during the internship include an opening/closing event, speaker series, community engagement, and general networking opportunities. Interns are provided with relevant work and case study material to enhance their skillset and prepare for a future in IB. If you are interested in a career in investment banking, this is the internship for you! Department: Corporate and Leveraged Finance Americas Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (“CACIB”) is the corporate and investment banking arm of the Crédit Agricole Group. Based in New York, CACIB’s Corporate and Leveraged Finance Group (“CLF”) includes Corporate Origination Americas that originates, structures, and distributes syndicated loans and bilateral facilities for the Americas as well as The Leveraged, Acquisition and Telecom Finance Group (“LATFG”) originates leveraged finance solutions for financial sponsors and corporates through leveraged loans and high yield bonds.. Furthermore, the Group acts as a primary underwriter and is active in the secondary markets to provide liquidity to investors. CLF is seeking a student in their penultimate within interest in the Financial Industry. CLF provides a full array of financing solutions for corporate clients and financial sponsors. The team originates, structures and distributes investment grade and leveraged debt financings, including investment grade and leveraged loans, high yield bonds, and bridge financings across general corporate and various structured finance sectors. This person will provide support to both junior and senior bankers, assist in financial modeling and credit analysis, analyze corporate credit ratings, conduct market research, and provide general support across various projects. The role offers an opportunity to assist in all aspects of deal execution and become an integral part of Credit Agricole’s CLF franchise. The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong work ethic and initiative, excellent analytical and communication skills, superior organizational ability, and the capacity to work under pressure. An understanding of banking and capital markets would be preferred. The position offers exposure across various groups/platforms across the bank and the opportunity to see syndicated loan, Term Loan B and HY bond transactions executed from beginning to end. Job Overview: Assist Corporate Origination and LATFG team members and management in the day-to-day tasks and responsibilities of the department, with a focus on Loan and Bond Origination. Prepare presentation materials including marketing information and internal reporting documents as well as the maintenance and updating of various data bases utilizing financial analysis skills. Responsibilities:Assist in preparation of presentation materials including pitch books, information memorandum and institutional investor / lender’s presentation materialsPrepare financial analysis on companies including ratio analysis, comparables and financial models with projectionsAssist in the preparation of transaction memorandums, credit analysis, and corporate credit ratings analysisCraft clear and succinct written analysis of market trends and commentaryMaintenance of databases and market comparablesReview of legal documentation and preparation of Closing MemosWork with other team members, credit, legal, relationship managers, operations and senior management to ensure the timely and accurate information gathering and analysis Assist in the preparation of weekly and monthly new market updates Qualifications:Student in their penultimate (junior) year of study, interested in a Finance career Applicant is eligible to work in the USApplicant will not require visa sponsorship now or in the future (F1, OPT, CPT)Strong interpersonal skills and ability to multi-taskStrong computer skills including use of Excel, PowerPoint, Word, BloombergFamiliarity with banking and capital markets a plusSome accounting/finance/economics coursework

jobs.description: Employer: Forbidden Well Expires: 10/22/2026 Marketing & Growth Lead (Paid Internship → Full-Time)Forbidden Well · New York, NY · Hybrid, 2 days a week on site$1,500/month · 90-day paid internship, designed to convert to full-time This is a six-figure job on the other side of 90 days.The internship pays $1,500/month. The full-time role it converts into starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and the revenue you generate. We built the path that way on purpose — we'd rather pay it out than not. You will own marketing. All of it.This is not an internship where you're handed a task list and asked to schedule someone else's posts. You will own the strategy, the calendar, the campaigns and the creative. The concepts are yours. The pitch ideas are yours. The call on what we run next is yours.We'll work alongside you to stay aligned on direction and make sure you have what you need, but you are not waiting on us to tell you what to do. If you need someone to hand you assignments, this is the wrong job. If you've been waiting for someone to hand you the keys instead, read on. You are the keeper of the brandForbidden Well should look and sound like one thing everywhere we show up: email campaigns, social posts, stories, the grid, and every other form of communication we put out. Someone should be able to see any piece of our content and know instantly that it's us.That means more than staying consistent. You'll continuously fine-tune that identity, stay organized in how we market, and be deliberate about what goes out and why. No random posting. Every piece has a purpose you can explain.You own every external relationshipThis role owns all points of contact with other spas, vendors, modeling agencies and brands — curating them, organizing them, and keeping them alive over time.A real example: a friend recently connected us to the owner of a very successful spa in Miami. We make the introduction, and from there it's yours to develop into something lucrative — a referral partnership where their clients coming to New York come to us, and ours heading to Miami go to them. First introduction to signed, working partnership, end to end. That's the job. What you'll runBrand, content and social across Instagram and TikTok: your concepts, your voice, your calendarBrand consistency across every channel we touch, and the standards that keep it that wayEmail marketing, including weekly campaigns and automated flowsPaid social and lead generation campaigns with our agency partnerPartnerships and outreach: spas, vendors, modeling agencies and like-minded brands, plus the co-marketing campaigns that come out of themPhoto and video shoots: concept, casting, scheduling and running the dayOur podcast, using our full in-house studio: booking guests, recording, editing and publishingLocal search, our Google Business Profile and our Google reviews programDaily and weekly reporting on what's working Who this is forYou generate ideas without being asked and can defend themYou write well and have taste. You can tell the difference between good and almost goodYou have an eye for consistency and it bothers you when something is off-brandYou're comfortable talking to people and turning an introduction into a relationship that lastsYou're comfortable with AI tools, especially Claude, and use them to move fasterYou're organized enough to run a shoot, a podcast taping and three campaigns in the same weekYou want to build something, not pad a resume Where it goesThis 90-day period is a prerequisite for a full-time, long-term role, and it's how we both find out if this is the right fit. We're hiring for the person who runs marketing at Forbidden Well for years — someone who grows as the company does and takes on more as we open more. If you hit the benchmarks, which we'll set with you and review together, the full-time role starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and revenue generated. About usForbidden Well is a luxury wellness house in New York built around IV therapy, advanced treatments and a client experience that feels like nothing else in the city.Apply with your resume and anything you've made that you're proud of: content, campaigns, a brand you built, a project that worked. Tell us about one brand whose identity you think is airtight and why, and one relationship or partnership you started and kept going. We care more about what you've shipped than where you've interned.

jobs.title: Stanley A. Weiss Internship Winter/Spring 2027 at Business Executives for National Security
jobs.description: Employer: Business Executives for National Security Expires: 10/22/2026 The Stanley A. Weiss Internship program places high-performing candidates at the intersection of industry and national security. Interns work full time (40 hrs/week) to support Business Executives for National Security (BENS) in our mission to apply industry experience and best business practices to address the U.S.’s most pressing national security challenges. Interns will have the opportunity to contribute directly to BENS' three campaigns, each of which guide our work and partner engagement: Homeland Resilience and Response: The private sector plays an increasingly central role in protecting the American homeland. BENS brings business expertise to bear on national security challenges, working across domains and with key government partners to develop innovative public-private partnerships, secure critical infrastructure, improve domain awareness, respond to economic coercion, and foster energy resilience.Strengthening Supply Chains: The U.S. is overexposed to supply chain disruption. BENS is working to identify opportunities to strengthen U.S. and allied supply chains to build a more resilient national security industrial base. Current lines of effort include leveraging private sector insight to support state-level national security initiatives, scaling emerging technologies, and improving U.S. biosecurity.Mobilizing Private Capital: National security priorities increasingly depend on private investment to accelerate industrial capacity, finance the defense industrial base at scale, and modernize critical infrastructure. BENS connects private capital with these priorities by helping senior leaders think creatively about policies and tools to mobilize private investment, and by expanding the community of investors familiar with national security opportunities. Recognizing that threats to U.S. national security rarely stay within traditional borders, BENS also engages in programmatic work focused on broader geopolitical dynamics relevant to U.S. interests. BENS has long supported U.S. combatant commands and NATO strategic commands by examining business and economic conditions pertinent to their respective missions:Geopolitics and Economic Statecraft: BENS engages senior business and government leaders at the intersection of geopolitics and economic security. A signature element of this workstream is BENS' executive travel program, which brings private sector leaders to examine and offer insights on critical geopolitical issues. At the request of U.S. government partners and allies, BENS has sent delegations in recent years to Brussels, Athens, Hanoi, Buenos Aires, and Panama City.PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIESStanley A. Weiss Interns are essential members of the BENS team, contributing to the organization’s goals by working closely with government partners and BENS members within the national security community.Interns will:Gain subject matter expertise in a national security topic through in-depth research and presentations to BENS senior leadership.Track and analyze relevant policy developments focused on critical infrastructure, geopolitics and economic statecraft, the national security industrial base, and emerging technology. Support BENS staff in outreach and engagement with national security-focused government partners and business leaders. Assist with event preparation, including producing preparatory materials, supporting logistics, and working with event participants. Draft and edit pieces for the BENS Substack, external articles, member-led reports, and partner-facing memos.Attend, take notes on, and analyze Congressional hearings, external events, and key meetings with government and private sector stakeholders.Maintain and update membership databases.Set up and break down office events.Provide general administrative support. REQUIREMENTS Education and ExperienceCandidates are evaluated based on their skills and prior experience. Most successful applicants have recently completed, or are in the process of completing, an undergraduate or graduate degree. SkillsSelf-starting, entrepreneurial approach to work and a genuine curiosity to explore new subject areas and sectors. Strong research, writing, and organizational skills. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely to diverse audiences. Ability to manage multiple priorities and excel in a fast-paced environment. Exceptional interpersonal and professional skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior business executives, military and government officials, and staff at partner organizations. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team. Proficiency with standard office software and digital research tools.Candidates with prior coursework, research, or professional interest in areas such as critical infrastructure, economic security, private capital, emerging technologies, the defense industrial base, critical supply chains, and/or critical minerals are encouraged to apply, though this experience is not required. TERMThe spring internship will begin in the early January and end in mid-May. Interns are paid an hourly wage set at the current D.C. minimum wage and receive metro travel benefits. Interns are expected to work full time, though exceptions may be made for outstanding candidates with academic conflicts.TO APPLYTo apply, submit your resume and written responses through this form. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so early submission is encouraged. The final deadline to apply is Friday October 30 at 5:00 pm ET.

jobs.description: Employer: Applied Industrial Technologies - Corporate Expires: 10/22/2026 We are currently seeking an intern to join our Applied Industrial Technologies (AIT) Accounting/Finance Department as part of a year-long rotational program (approximately June 2020– May 2021). The person will rotate between six different departments within Accounting-Finance (approximately two months in each department). This will allow the individual to experience a variety of aspects of Accounting and Finance and better understand how each department helps support and drive the business. The internship program is flexible and hours can be established to accommodate the student’s class schedule. The expectation is that the intern will be full-time (40 hrs/week) in the summer and part-time during the winter/spring (being able to work 16-24 hrs/week). This position could involve limited travel during the summer (domestic only). JOB DUTIES (Listed by Department) Internal Audit - Test key SOX controls at AIT Corporate and specific Subsidiaries in order to properly assess the design and operating effectiveness of the control. This will also include operational controls and controls related to configuration (mainly SAP) that drive system functionality and business processes. Perform audit procedures, including identifying issues, reviewing and analyzing evidence, conducting interviews, and documenting the results of the procedures performed & conclusions reached. Will also compile audit findings and recommendations for modifications and improvements to processes and systems. Communicate corrective actions when necessary.General Accounting – Participate in monthly close process. Research cost center general ledger posting inquires. jobs.title: MBA Marketing Intern at Graco Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 10/22/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned. What You Will Bring to Graco Currently pursuing an MBA, with an expected graduation date within 12–18 months of the internship Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field Prior experience in marketing, business strategy, or vertical-specific market development (internship or professional) preferred Team collaborator with experience working in multi-functional or global team settings Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and synthesize VOC insights and market research into clear recommendations Excellent communication and presentation skills, including comfort presenting to senior leadership Ability to manage ambiguity and drive a project forward with limited day-to-day direction

jobs.title: Swine Intern at Waukon Feed Ranch
jobs.description: Employer: Waukon Feed Ranch Expires: 10/22/2026 Position Overview: This role involves working on a modern, state-of-the-art farrow-to-wean sow farm. It's an exciting opportunity for an ambitious individual looking to kickstart their career in the swine industry and gain hands-on experience in Swine Research & Training. This is a 12-week internship. Research Project Description Intern will help create staff training videos while completing a measurable research project, choosing from topics such as Piglet Welfare Management (e.g., separating piglets for colostrum access vs. drying piglets, or drying piglets vs. assisting the sow), Farrowing rate analysis based on sow condition scores, or Sow mortality tracking in relation to condition scores. This allows intern to apply practical skills, collect data, and generate insights that support animal welfare and herd performance. Findings will be presented to the WFR Swine Management team. Essential Job Responsibilities Learn and apply WFR core values and contribute to a positive culture. Complete and take ownership of required research project Experience all areas of a modern sow systems including farrowing, gestation, forecasting, reporting, and more Ensuring all animals are receiving proper feed, water, and ventilation Shipping and receiving animals Treating animals Heat checking and breeding sows and gilts via artificial insemination Assisting with the birthing process of sows and gilts including sleeving Caring for piglets and ensuring they are off to a good start Moving animals with a sort board Cleaning facilities including power-washing, disinfecting, scraping manure, picking up cleanings, and removing deceased animals Weaning piglets from their mothers and giving wean shots Processing piglets including castration, docking tails, tattooing, and giving injections Following the proper steps for timely euthanasia Pen management, culling, sorting Keeping detailed, accurate records that comply with integrator Collect and send blood, saliva, fecal, fluid, and tissue samples for testing as needed. Experience multiple sow farms as well as other WFR departments Assist in creating clear and professional training videos to support farm staff education Maintain confidentiality regarding company information, employee information, production information, biosecurity practices, and other proprietary or confidential information. Understand & follow WFR's biosecurity protocol, including showering in and out of the facility when visiting production sites Understand & follow WFR's animal welfare policy Understand & follow WFR's handbook and procedures Work cooperatively and respectfully with a diverse team, contributing to a positive, professional, and team-oriented work environment. Maintain PQA+ certification Reasonable Accommodations Statement: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties of the position. Education and Experience Currently enrolled at a college or university, pursuing a degree in agriculture, veterinary science, or a related field. Qualifications Strong interest in agriculture and animals with a desire to learn and self-develop Self-motivated team player with a positive attitude Strong prioritization and organizational skills Effectively communicate with team members Strong written and verbal communication skills with attention to grammar, accuracy, and detail Physical Requirements Frequently stand, walk, and be on feet for extended periods, typically 8 to 10 hours a day, including concrete, slatted flooring, and wet or uneven surfaces Occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull a minimum of 50 lbs., and occasionally more with assistance Frequently bend, stoop, reach, squat, and kneel while working with animals and equipment Capable of repeated actions, including handling animals, tools, and equipment Occasionally climb stairs and ladders and work in confined or low-clearance areas within barns and production facilities Ability to comply with biosecurity requirements, including showering in and out of the facility and wearing required personal protective equipment Sufficient vision, hearing, and speech to safely handle animals, monitor health, and communicate clearly in a noisy farm environment Work Environment Schedule: This is a 12-week internship with full-time hours (40-45 hours per week) available each week of the internship. Interns must work scheduled days and hours and are expected to be punctual and reliable. Environment: Primarily a hog farm setting, both indoors and outdoors, with dusty conditions. Noise level is usually moderate to loud. Travel: Occasional travel to meetings or other farm sites; overall travel requirements are limited. Please note that this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of duties or responsibilities. Duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

jobs.description: Employer: City and County of Denver Expires: 10/22/2026 DENTERN– Systems Integration Management Office (SIMO) - Denver International Airport Who We AreSince opening on Feb. 28, 1995, Denver International Airport (DEN) has become one of the world’s busiest airports. In 2025, 82,427,962 passengers passed through DEN, making DEN 4th busiest airport in the U.S. and the world’s 10th busiest airport. DEN is Colorado’s primary economic engine, generating $47.2 billion in annual economic impact for the state. At DEN, we are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We celebrate individuality and strive to keep Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Accessibility (EDIA) at the center of all that we do. What We OfferThis internship is an on-call position, which means it is a part-time, hourly role. The City and County of Denver offers a competitive pay rate to commensurate with education, with the pay range for this position between $19.75 to $22.34 per hour. This position is eligible to enroll in the City and County of Denver’s 457b retirement plan. This position is not eligible for other additional benefits. On-call positions may have routine or variable work schedules. Denver International Airport's emerging talent positions require DENterns to participate in a cohort-based model that emphasizes networking, collaboration, and professional growth, attending all scheduled professional development sessions, tours, and engaging in impactful projects across the airport. What You'll DoThe Denver International Airport (DEN) Systems Integration Management Office (SIMO) is actively seeking a DENtern to contribute to its division, which plays a crucial role in ensuring seamless integration across airport operations, enhancing operational efficiency, and fostering enterprise-wide collaboration. Within the Chief of Staff’s portfolio, the office will serve as the central hub, providing proactive, hands-on leadership. It will ensure that capital and program management, operations, maintenance, and customer service are seamlessly integrated into a cohesive ecosystem. At Denver International Airport, Systems Integration Management is the practice of connecting people, projects, operations, stakeholders, and decisions across one of the world's most complex airport environments. SIMO helps align work across organizational boundaries, coordinate enterprise priorities, and ensure initiatives are implemented as part of a connected system rather thanas independent efforts. Drawing from disciplines such as systems integration, program integration, organizational readiness, governance, and continuous improvement, SIMO helps the airport deliver outcomes that no single department could achieve alone. As an intern, you will gain experience working on projects such as: Coordinating program development and implementation steps in the exploration, initiation, and testing of leading-edge ideas resulting from Leadership DEN and Eno AirMAX Capstone Projects. Conducting assessments and making recommendations related to DEN multi-sector stakeholders and related projects. Developing and implementing an enterprise-wide communication plan related to the DEN-wide goals and objectives of SIMO. Providing technical support to SIMO management on DEN plans, programs, and projects in the development of comprehensive reports, correspondence, and cost estimates to executive and management staff, City Council, Mayor’s Office, and outside regulatory agencies. What You'll Bring We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level. Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics: Interest in public service and enhancing customer experience in the aviation industry. Knowledge of public administration, social, political, and environmental issues influencing the aviation industry. Strong organizational and project management skills. Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholder groups. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Initiative, resiliency, and adaptability to changing circumstances and deadlines within a dynamic organization and evolving industry. Creativity and innovation in problem-solving. Well-developed listening, communication, writing, and organizational skills. Attention to detail and the ability to seek guidance on assignments prior to deadlines. Sound judgment, creativity, and innovation in decision-making. To be successful, our ideal candidate also: Maintains a high degree of integrity and respect for self and others. Prioritizes values-driven customer service. Is committed to learning and is not afraid to seek constructive feedback to improve. Is intentional about being empathetic, kind, and flexible with teammates and superiors. Keeps an open mind and has a sense of purpose. Enjoys a sense of humor Location Flexibility The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model with a required 3 days in the office. This position will report to our brand-new Gateway Building and employee parking will be provided. Employees work where needed to support the business at the Denver International Airport. We do not offer housing or relocation assistance for this position. Internship Duration and Hours This internship is expected to continue through May 2027. Hours will vary based on business needs, with a typical schedule ranging from 20 to 30 hours per week, not to exceed 39 hours in any given week. The intern’s work schedule will be flexible to accommodate their current academic commitments. Minimum Qualifications Education Requirement: Current enrollment in an accredited college program leading to a certificate, licensure, associate's, bachelor’s, or other higher degree, or a recent graduate (completed specified program within 1 year of completion). Experience: None Education and Experience Equivalency: No substitution of experience for education is permitted. Mandatory documentation required to be considered for this position: Resume (with most current information) Transcripts – either official or unofficial; dated within your current academic term. This is used only to verify credit amounts; grades will not influence the decision. Additional document (optional, but highly encouraged): Cover letter detailing why you are interested in this position. Application Deadline This position is expected to stay open until Friday, 10/16. Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than Friday, 10/16 at 11:59 PM. The City and County of Denver provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, genetic information, age, or any other status protected under federal, state, and/or local law. FBI Background Check FBI criminal background check is required for all positions at Denver International Airport (DEN). Employees are also required to report any felony convictions and/or moving violations to maintain this clearance and be eligible for continued employment. By position, a pre-employment physical/drug test may be required. For information about right to work, click here for English or here for Spanish.

The Metropolitan Councils made up of several operating divisions that service the Twin Cities Metropolitan area in a number of ways. You will contribute to communities, the region, and the nation by conducting economic research, participating in monetary policy-making, supervising certain financial institutions, providing financial services and payments, playing a leadership role in the payments industry, and supporting economic well-being in communities through a variety of efforts. jobs.title: Data Science Internship (Summer 2027) at Battelle
jobs.description: Employer: Battelle Expires: 10/24/2026 For brilliant minds in science, technology, engineering and business operations, Battelle is the place to do the greatest good by solving humanity’s most pressing challenges and creating a safer, healthier and more secure world. At Battelle, interns and co-ops make an impact through hands-on learning and exciting and challenging projects. Our interns are an integral part of the teams they support and will feel like they are a true, valued team member. We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply. A brighter future is possible with you.Job SummaryBattelle’s Mission Focused Tools Division is responsible for developing unique embedded security solutions for government and industrial customers. We are currently seeking a Data Science Intern for Summer 2027. This position is onsite in Columbus, OH. As a Data Science Intern, you will work with a diverse group of people from many quantitative disciplines such as physics, computer science, electrical engineering, statistics, systems biology, and mathematics. We work with a variety of data such as microelectronic images and schematics, signal data, text corpuses, ontologies, networks, and simulation results. Interest in cybersecurity or tactical autonomy is a must, but experience is not necessary. No matter where you start from, we value your unique perspective and have a culture that supports continual learning, creativity, and risk taking. As a Data Science Intern, you will work on a variety of data-driven problems using cutting edge machine learning, statistics, and data analytics. Many of our projects require developing new methods, and the ideal candidate will be comfortable learning outside of their expertise, conceptualizing a problem, and thinking deeply about data and what it can tell us. We welcome your unique academic and commercial experience in machine learning, statistics, mathematical modeling, data mining and munging, network analysis, natural language processing, data analytics, or physical system simulation. However, the most important skills are enthusiasm for learning and data-driven problem solving.ResponsibilitiesIntern activities may include some or all of the following: Develop and maintain data processing and analysis solutions. Leverage Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing techniques to support technology assessments and technical reporting.Aid in the design and implementation of machine learning and data engineering techniques applied to cyber security problems, supply chain security, internet of things (IoT), and commercial platforms.Assist in the iterative design and counter design process of tactical simulationsImprove existing techniques and devise new techniques to solve security data problemsUse Generative AI agents to solve unique data problems such as planning and coordinationIdentify and articulate strengths and weaknesses of solutions, conclusions, and problem approaches during technical discussionsLearn and become fluent in the details of security related domains to devise data driven solutionsKey QualificationsMust be currently pursuing bachelor’s or master's degree in a field which demonstrates analytical sophistication (Statistics, Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, Quantitative Social Sciences, Computational Biology or similar)Must have experience developing in Python, through classwork, commercial experience, or similarExcitement about learning new technical subject area and curiosity about cybersecurity problemsCommunication and teamwork skillsMust be a U.S. Citizen with ability to obtain government security clearanceCompensation DataThe salary range for this role is $20.00 – $40.00 per hour, in addition to a $2,000 housing stipend for students relocating more than 50 miles from home and university. Internship pay is benchmarked against national averages taking into consideration a student's major and year in school. Preparing You for Career Success The Battelle intern and co-op program is a great way to increase experience both on a team and as an independent contributor. Ninety-eight percent of internship survey respondents said they felt better prepared to enter the workforce after their Battelle internship and 100% said they were treated with respect by their colleagues. You will have the opportunity to thrive in a culture that inspires you to:Apply your talent to challenging and meaningful projects Pursue ideas in scientific and technological discovery Partner with world-class experts in a collaborative environmentBecome the next generation of scientific leaders and business professionals Are you ready to help solve the most important challenges of today and tomorrow? If so, we are ready to support you with:Flexible work schedules: Most teams follow a flexible, compressed work schedule that allows for every other Friday offEnjoy enhanced work flexibility, including a hybrid arrangement: You have options for where and when you work. Our Together with Flexibility model allows you to work 60% in-office and 40% remote, with Monday and Tuesday as common in-office days, dependent on team and position needs.Employee Resource Groups that help cultivate an inclusive and welcoming communitySocial and professional networking events with Battelle Senior Leadership and your colleaguesOpportunities for philanthropic involvement to give back and make an impact in the community

As North America’s largest total beverage distributor, Southern Glazer’s isn't just one of Forbes’ Top Private Companies; it's a family-owned business with deep roots dating back to 1933.Southern Glazer’s is proud of its well-earned positive reputation, continually achieving accolades for our outstanding workplace culture. We take pride in creating a culture where our people are valued, supported, and provided opportunities for growth and belonging. By joining Southern Glazer’s, you would be part of a team that values excellence, innovation, and community. This is more than just a job – it's an opportunity to build the future of beverage distribution and grow with a company that truly cares about its people. Southern Glazer’s offers a competitive compensation package with an hourly pay rate of $25 / hour. In determining a final offer, the company will evaluate a specific candidate's education, skills and experience and will make an offer appropriately. OverviewThe Southern Glazer’s Internship Program was established to develop the next generation of Technology leaders. Each summer, the program offers interns the opportunity to engage in career building activities while simultaneously learning and applying industry-leading practices.This hands-on experience gives interns the chance to explore and understand the adult beverage industry. The knowledge gained from industry leaders will allow you to build a network of professionals within the beverage alcohol industry and here at Southern Glazer’s. Being a Southern Glazer’s intern means you’ll be invited to our Leadership Spotlight Series, a Community Service Day exclusive to our intern class, as well as access to Professional Development workshops and trainings!Primary ResponsibilitiesAs a OneTech Intern, you’ll work in a variety of Digital and Technology areas, including but not limited to: Enterprise Products & Platforms, Data & Analytics, Infrastructure & Ops, Cybersecurity, and Digital Strategy, to gain knowledge and understanding of technology’s role in the wine and spirits distribution industry. This role will be specifically working with the Data Science team, focusing on a variety of projects. The structured internship is designed to expose students to the wine and spirits Three-Tier beverage distribution system and the role technology plays to enable business capabilities. Interns will finish the program having gained broad experience in various aspects of the relationship between technology, sales and operations. Part of the experience will include supporting projects as assigned and defined by student’s specific learning goals, participating in training, on-site meetings, and department wide learning opportunities as available. Lastly, interns will complete an end of internship project showcasing one’s knowledge and present to management. jobs.description: Employer: SiteOne Landscape Supply Expires: 10/24/2026 SiteOne associates are customer obsessed, always safe, continuously improving, and having fun! Whether you are experienced in the green industry, a professional looking for a career change, or a new graduate or veteran transitioning into the workforce, we are confident you will find opportunity and reward with SiteOne. SiteOne Landscape Supply is the largest and only national wholesale distributor of landscaping products in the United States and Canada. With over 700 branches across the U.S. and Canada, we offer a comprehensive selection of products including: irrigation supplies, fertilizer and control products, nursery goods, hardscapes, landscape lighting, drainage and erosion control products, tools, and other landscaping accessories and supplies. SiteOne Landscape Supply offers a progressive style internship program designed to give students hands on experience in all facets of our branch operations. jobs.title: VESTER Campus Ambassador at Golden Hire Consulting
jobs.description: Employer: Golden Hire Consulting Expires: 10/24/2026 Join the Founding Team at VESTERYou buy a coffee at Starbucks. Instead of earning points, you earn Starbucks stock.That’s VESTER.VESTER powers stockback rewards — infrastructure that enables brands to reward customers with their own stock instead of traditional loyalty points.We’re growing quickly and hand-selecting some of the sharpest, most connected students on campus to help introduce VESTER to the next generation of investors and consumers.Why Join VESTER? Work Directly With the FoundersReceive direct mentorship from VESTER’s founding team, with experience spanning Société Générale, J.P. Morgan, and Goldman Sachs. There’s no middle layer — you’ll work closely with the people building the company. Get Paid for GrowthEarn compensation for every classmate you successfully sign up, with additional bonuses for reaching growth milestones.Learn Fintech, Markets & SalesGain hands-on exposure to how financial markets, fintech startups, customer acquisition, and enterprise sales operate before your first major internship. Build Your RésuméAdd meaningful startup experience to your résumé while becoming one of the first students involved with VESTER.Top-performing ambassadors will also receive early access to future opportunities as the company scales.Exclusive VESTER MerchRepresent VESTER on campus with exclusive company merchandise and ambassador gear, available to members of the campus ambassador team.Who We’re Looking ForYou might be a strong fit if:You’re connected. You’re active in clubs, Greek life, sports teams, student organizations, residence halls, or campus group chats.You’re curious. You’re interested in markets, investing, fintech, startups, or entrepreneurship. Prior experience is not required.You’re growth-minded. You take initiative, experiment with new ideas, and enjoy figuring out how to get people excited about something new.You’re an operator. You don’t wait around for instructions — you find opportunities and execute.You’re a student. Freshmen and sophomores are especially encouraged to apply, although juniors and seniors are welcome.What You’ll DoAs a VESTER Campus Ambassador, you’ll help grow VESTER within your university community by:Introducing students to VESTER and the concept of stockback rewardsDriving student sign-ups through your campus networkBuilding awareness through clubs, organizations, teams, and student communitiesTesting creative campus growth strategiesSharing feedback directly with VESTER’s founding teamHelping shape VESTER’s early campus growth strategyWhy Now?VESTER is only selecting a handful of ambassadors per campus.Joining now means getting involved at an early stage, working directly with the founding team, and helping shape how VESTER grows across universities.The strongest candidates will be considered first.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Planning Analyst at Cleveland-Cliffs
jobs.description: Employer: Cleveland-Cliffs Expires: 10/24/2026 Cleveland-Cliffs takes pride in offering a variety of opportunities for students and new graduates who have an interest in the steel industry and a passion for innovation and sustainability. We offer a best-in-class internship program in the industry and partner with many universities to provide co-op opportunities. Working beside industry-leading engineering and operational leaders, our interns/co-ops will create meaningful solutions to real-world problems. As an intern/co-op with Cleveland-Cliffs, you will build life-long professional connections and have the opportunity to be considered for future full-time employment. As a Manufacturing Planning Analyst Intern at Cleveland-Cliffs, the projects assigned will vary based on the intern’s education level and plant location, but will generally reflect the duties outlined below. Summary of Responsibilities:Building production schedules to support customer delivery expectationsManagement of WIP inventoriesWork closely with Sales, Operations management, and accounting in the planning/scheduling of operating units and expediting of customer ordersUtilize Microsoft Excel and Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio to find, retrieve, filter, and validate dataPopulate and issue standard daily/weekly/monthly reportingProvide analysis from various aspects of the operation that can take extreme detail, and create a story with themes that clearly show issues and required actionsSupport the monthly and annual production forecast planning processAutomate work currently done manually in Excel and utilize the task scheduler application to maintain existing automated reportsSupport the company-wide delivery improvement initiativeVarious other duties as needed to support the businessMinimum Qualifications:Enrollment in Bachelor of Science program in the field of Supply Chain, Business, or another Business-related fieldCompletion of sophomore year of study by the summer of 2027 Applicants for this position must be currently legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Cleveland-Cliffs is a leading North America-based steel producer with focus on value-added sheet products, particularly for the automotive industry. The Company is vertically integrated from the mining of iron ore, production of pellets and direct reduced iron, and processing of ferrous scrap through primary steelmaking and downstream finishing, stamping, tooling, and tubing. We offer an excellent total compensation package, including competitive pay with variable compensation opportunity, health insurance, retirement plan, education assistance, paid time off, and more. Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please send an e-mail to careers@clevelandcliffs.com or call 1-(312) 899-3097 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Do not email your application materials to this email address. Application materials sent to this email address will not be considered. Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. is an equal opportunity employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. We are a drug-free workplace and conduct pre-employment screening as a condition of employment.
